column4: We, His followers, are to *“go and make disciples of all nations.”* Discipleship is about personal growth and about multiplying that growth by teaching others to follow Christ. Discipleship is the vehicle through which we build the Kingdom of God; the teachings of Jesus are the message.
column5: As His followers, we are to *“go and make disciples of all nations.”* Discipleship is about personal growth and also about multiplying that growth by teaching others to follow Christ. Discipleship is the vehicle by which we build God’s kingdom; Jesus’ teaching is the message.

column4: The call to be a disciple is more than attending church or learning Bible verses-it is an invitation to live like Jesus and to partner with Him in advancing God’s Kingdom. Genuine discipleship helps believers become spiritually mature and effective for ministry (Ephesians 4:13). It shapes both the heart and skills needed to serve others and share the Gospel. As Paul instructed Timothy in 2 Timothy 2:2, discipleship follows a pattern of spiritual multiplication, where trained disciples continue raising up new followers to lead other to Christ.
column5: The call to be a disciple is not merely to attend church or memorize Bible verses-it is an invitation to live like Jesus and to partner with Him in advancing God’s kingdom. True discipleship helps believers mature spiritually and become more effective in ministry (Ephesians 4:13). It shapes the mindset and skills needed to serve others and share the gospel. As Paul taught Timothy in 2 Timothy 2:2, discipleship follows a pattern of spiritual multiplication, where trained disciples continue to raise up new followers and lead others to Christ.

column4: Discipleship is both an individual calling and a global mission. On a personal level, it involves growing in faith, developing an active spiritual life, being in relationship with others & God. At the same time, it fuels the mission of the Church to reach every nation with the Gospel, ensuring that the message of Christ continues to expand and transform lives across generations.
column5: Discipleship is both a personal calling and a global mission. On a personal level, it involves growth in faith, developing a vibrant spiritual life, and building relationships with others and with God. At the same time, it propels the church to reach the nations with the gospel, ensuring that Christ’s message continues to expand and transform lives across generations.

column4: ## Why Discipleship Matters
column5: ## Why Discipleship Matters

column4: The impact of discipleship goes beyond personal transformation-it has a Kingdom impact. Paul reminded Timothy in 2 Timothy 2:2 to entrust what He had learned to faithful men who would then teach others also. This generational pattern highlights how discipleship is the engine that drives the growth and sustainability of the Church. Discipleship matters because it was Jesus’ chosen method for spreading the Gospel and building His Church.
column5: The impact of discipleship goes beyond personal change-it brings kingdom impact. In 2 Timothy 2:2, Paul reminds Timothy to entrust what he has learned to faithful people who will be able to teach others also. This generational pattern shows that discipleship is the engine driving the church’s growth and endurance. Discipleship matters because it is the method Jesus chose to spread the gospel and build His church.

column4: Rather than focusing on large crowds, Jesus intentionally invested in a small group of followers, teaching them, modeling faithfulness, and preparing them to carry forward His mission. This personal, relational approach ensured that His message would multiply, as each disciple was equipped to make more disciples.
column5: Jesus did not focus on massive crowds, but intentionally cultivated a small group of followers, teaching them, modeling faithfulness for them, and preparing them to carry on His mission. This personal, relational approach ensured that His message would multiply, because each disciple was equipped to bring forth more disciples.

column4: At its core, discipleship is central to fulfilling the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20). Jesus did not just call us to make converts but to make disciples-followers who are grounded in God’s Word, empowered by the Holy Spirit, and equipped for ministry. Through discipleship, believers grow in their knowledge of Scripture, develop spiritual disciplines, and learn to walk in obedience to Christ. It prepares the Church to impact the world, advance the Gospel, and reflect the glory of God to all nations.
column5: Essentially, discipleship is at the heart of fulfilling the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20). Jesus calls us not merely to decisions of faith but to make disciples-these followers are rooted in God’s Word, empowered by the Holy Spirit, and equipped for ministry. Through discipleship, believers grow in their understanding of Scripture, establish spiritual disciplines, and learn to walk in obedience to Christ. Discipleship prepares the church to impact the world, advance the gospel, and reflect God’s glory among the nations.

column4: ### Nature vs Nurture
column5: ### Nature and Nurture

column4: In the study of biology, psychology, and anthropology we often consider the impact of nature versus nurture. The question often posed, is a person more the result of their innate, in-built genetic heritage? Or are they more the result of their environment and upbringing? The truth is that every person is a blend of nature and nurture. Both elements in strong interplay choreograph the development of a human soul.
column5: In studies of biology, psychology, and anthropology, we often consider the influence of nature and nurture. People often ask whether a person is shaped more by inborn genetic inheritance, or more by environment and upbringing. The truth is that everyone is a fusion of nature and nurture. These two factors interact powerfully, together composing the growth of a person’s soul.

column4: When you accepted Jesus, the miracle of salvation made you born-again of incorruptible seed. You received a godly nature! Your spiritual DNA was re-written! This godly nature causes a stirring in our hearts to be close to our heavenly Father, to know Him, to experience Him.
column5: When you receive Jesus, the miracle of salvation causes you to be born again by that imperishable seed. You receive a godly nature! Your spiritual DNA is rewritten! This godly nature stirs our hearts to draw near to the Father, to know Him, and to experience Him.

column4: Just as a new-born, whose wonderful, beautiful, innocent nature must be shaped by loving parents to develop into a healthy and mature individual, we too must be shaped and nurtured to be developed.
column5: Just as a newborn’s beautiful, lovely, innocent nature must be shaped by loving parents in order to grow into a healthy, mature person, we too must be formed and nourished in order to grow.

column4: Discipleship is the process of spiritual development that builds upon our godly nature and makes us spiritually mature. Through investing in discipleship, we ensure that faith is passed down, leaders are raised up, and the Church remains healthy and vibrant-both locally and globally.
column5: Discipleship is the spiritual growth process that builds upon our godly nature and brings us to spiritual maturity. By committing to discipleship, we ensure that the faith is passed on, leaders are raised up, and the church remains healthy and vibrant at both the local and global levels-whether locally or globally.

column4: ### Didactic Model vs Apprentice Model
column5: ### Didactic Model vs Apprenticeship Model

column4: In modern day western education, the primary relationship the student has is with the material. The student’s learning is focused on content, material, books, videos, assignments, etc. The transformation of education happens via the curriculum. This method of teaching is known as the *didactic model*.
column5: In contemporary Western education, a student’s primary relationship is with the curriculum. Students’ learning focuses on content, materials, books, videos, assignments, and so on. Educational change is achieved through courses. This instructional approach is called the *didactic model*.

column4: The paradigm of the didactic model has not always been the norm. The model and method used in Jesus’ age was the *apprentice model.* This model of learning emphasizes knowledge being more ‘caught than taught’ and focuses more on the relationship between student and teacher, than student and curriculum.
column5: The lecture-based model has not always been the norm. The model and method used in Jesus’ time was *the apprenticeship model.* This learning model emphasizes that knowledge is more “caught than taught,” and it focuses more on the relationship between student and teacher than on the relationship between student and curriculum.

column4: The didactic model gradually became the default method over about a millennium, from the first medieval universities of Europe in the 11<sup>th</sup> - 13<sup>th</sup> centuries, the invention of the printing press in the 15<sup>th</sup> century, the enlightenment of the 17<sup>th</sup> & 18<sup>th</sup> century, and the impact of industrial revolution on information and education in the 19<sup>th</sup> & 20<sup>th</sup> centuries.
column5: Over roughly a millennium, the lecture-based model gradually became the default method, from the earliest medieval universities in Europe in the 11<sup>th</sup> - 13<sup>th</sup> centuries, the invention of the printing press in the 15<sup>th</sup> century, the Enlightenment in the 17<sup>th</sup> & 18<sup>th</sup> centuries, and the impact of the Industrial Revolution on information and education in the 19<sup>th</sup> & 20<sup>th</sup> centuries.

column4: The advantage of the didactic model is that it can scale more efficiently than the apprentice model. Massively open online courses (MOOCs) can have thousands of students at the same time, whereas even a very skilled master can only have perhaps a few dozen apprentices concurrently.
column5: The advantage of the lecture-based model is that it is more efficient at scale than the apprenticeship model. Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) can host tens of thousands of students at once, whereas even a very skilled master can perhaps take on only dozens of apprentices at a time.

column4: The result of the didactic model is that the student has mastery of content, however the student does not become like the teacher. The teacher is a facilitator for the curriculum. The teacher imparts knowledge.
column5: The result of the lecture-based model is that students gain mastery of content; however, students do not become like the teacher. The teacher is the facilitator of the course. The teacher imparts knowledge.

column4: In the apprentice model the master shares more than knowledge, he imparts wisdom. The result of the apprentice model is that the student has become like the master so completely that the student can reproduce the work of the master and take on apprentices of his own.
column5: In the apprenticeship model, the master shares not only knowledge but imparts wisdom. The result of the apprenticeship model is that students become so completely like the master that they can reproduce the master’s work and take on apprentices of their own.

column4: The didactic model has its use and place in the Kingdom of God, a good example is this book or any other Christian educational material. Jesus as a rabbi, skilled and trained in the rabbinical method, practiced the apprentice model as the primary model for His disciples.

column4: ## Jesus’ Model and Process of Discipleship
column5: ## Jesus’ Discipleship Model and Process

column4: Jesus demonstrated the mature and complete example of discipleship in the Gospels with His chosen disciples. We should use these steps broadly as the foundation for our own walk in becoming and making disciples.
column5: In the Gospels, Jesus, together with the disciples He chose, demonstrated a mature and complete example of discipleship. We should broadly base our own path of being and making disciples on these steps.

column4: The apprentice model has two roles: master and student. Every master has been a student, and hopefully every student will become a master. I will use the terms *disciple* to refer to the student and *disciple-maker* to refer to the master/teacher.
column5: The apprenticeship model has two roles: master and student. Every master was once a student, and hopefully every student will become a master. I will use the term *disciple* for the student and *disciple-maker* for the master/teacher.

column4: Every discipleship relationship goes through a progression of eight phases. column4: ### Invitation/Calling
column5: ### Invitation/Call

column4: Discipleship begins with a personal invitation from Jesus to follow Him. In Matthew 4:19, Jesus called His first disciples, saying, *“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.”* This invitation was both relational and transformational-it required leaving behind old ways of life and stepping into a new purpose centered on God’s mission. Jesus’ call wasn’t to spectatorship but to participation in His ministry and Kingdom work.
column5: Discipleship begins with Jesus issuing a personal invitation to people to follow Him. In Matthew 4:19, Jesus called His first disciples, saying: *“Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.”* This invitation is both relational and transformative-it requires leaving behind an old way of life and entering a new purpose centered on God’s mission. Jesus’ call is not to be a spectator, but to participate in His ministry and Kingdom work.

column4: Modern disciple-makers must invite others into authentic relationships that inspire spiritual growth and obedience. The invitation to discipleship is deeply personal. Jesus meets individuals where they are, addressing their unique needs and circumstances, but He also calls them to go deeper-to grow, serve, and become more like Him. This pattern reflects the relational nature of discipleship, where the focus is not merely on knowledge but on a life-changing relationship with Christ.
column5: Contemporary disciple-makers must invite others into genuine relationships that spark spiritual growth and obedience. The invitation to discipleship is deeply personal. Jesus meets people in their circumstances, addressing their unique needs and situations, but He also calls them further- to grow, serve, and become more like Him. This pattern reflects the relational nature of discipleship, where the focus is not merely knowledge, but a life-changing relationship with Christ.

column4: ### Teaching
column5: ### Teaching

column4: Teaching is at the heart of discipleship. Jesus spent much of His ministry teaching the principles of the Kingdom of God, most notably in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7). His teachings provided a foundation for living righteously, loving others, and walking in obedience to God. Instruction in the Word of God remains central to discipleship today, as Scripture is the primary tool for spiritual growth, correction, and training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16-17).
column5: Teaching is central to discipleship. Jesus devoted much of His ministry to teaching the principles of the Kingdom of God, most notably in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7). His teaching provided a foundation for living righteously, loving others, and doing God’s will. In discipleship today, teaching God’s Word remains central, because Scripture is the primary tool for spiritual growth, correction, and training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16-17).

column4: Disciple-makers must commit to teaching the Bible faithfully, helping others understand and apply it to their lives. Teaching involves more than imparting knowledge-it requires modeling Christ-like living so disciples can see faith in action. Jesus embodied the truths He taught, showing that effective teaching is both verbal and visible. In the same way, disciple-makers should strive to live out what they teach, providing practical examples of obedience and faithfulness.
column5: Disciple-makers must be committed to faithfully teaching the Bible, helping others understand it and apply it to life. Teaching is not merely the transfer of knowledge-it requires modeling a Christlike life so that disciples can see faith in action. Jesus lived out the truths He taught, showing that effective teaching is both spoken and visible. Likewise, disciple-makers should strive to live what they teach, providing practical examples of obedience and faithfulness.

column4: ### Demonstrating
column5: ### Demonstration

column4: Jesus didn’t just teach His disciples- He demonstrated how to live out the truths He proclaimed. Jesus showed what it means to love, serve, and minister in practical ways. Some examples from the gospels are Jesus washing the disciples’ feet as an act of humility and service (John 13:12-15), healing the sick, and feeding the hungry. Through His actions, He modeled compassion, faith, and boldness, leaving a clear example for His followers to imitate.
column5: Jesus did not only teach His disciples- He also demonstrated how to live out the truths He proclaimed. Jesus showed in concrete ways what love, service, and ministry look like. Examples in the Gospels include: Jesus washing His disciples’ feet as an act of humility and service (John 13:12-15), healing the sick, and feeding the hungry. Through His actions, He set an example of compassion, faith, and courage, leaving His followers with a clear pattern to imitate.

column4: Discipleship requires showing, not just telling. Modern disciple-makers must be transparent about their faith journey, including struggles and victories, so others can see how faith works in real life. Whether it’s praying with someone in need, sharing testimonies, or serving the community, discipleship thrives when it’s rooted in practical demonstration. Actions often speak louder than words, making demonstration a powerful tool for training others in the faith.
column5: Discipleship requires showing, not just telling. Contemporary disciple-makers must be transparent about their journey of faith, including struggles and victories, so that others can see faith at work in real life. Whether praying with those in need, sharing testimonies, or serving the community, discipleship thrives when it is grounded in practical demonstration. Actions often speak louder than words, making demonstration a powerful tool for training others in the faith.

column4: ### Participation/Trying
column5: ### Participation/Trying

column4: Jesus didn’t keep His disciples on the sidelines- He actively involved them in ministry experiences. In Luke 9:1-6 and Matthew 10:5-15, Jesus sent the disciples out to preach the Gospel, heal the sick, and cast out demons. These hands-on opportunities allowed the disciples to learn by doing, gaining confidence and skills under His guidance.
column5: Jesus did not leave His disciples on the sidelines- He actively involved them in ministry experiences. In Luke 9:1-6 and Matthew 10:5-15, Jesus sent the disciples out to preach the gospel, heal the sick, and cast out demons. These hands-on opportunities allowed the disciples to learn by doing under His guidance, gaining confidence and skill.

column4: Modern discipleship should also include practical involvement. Disciple-makers must invite disciples to participate in ministry, whether through leading prayer groups, sharing testimonies, or serving in outreach events. Providing safe spaces for practice allows disciples to grow in boldness while being supported and encouraged. Learning happens best when it is applied, and participation is the key to turning theory into action.
column5: Modern discipleship should also include practical participation. Disciplers must invite disciples to engage in ministry, whether leading a prayer group, sharing testimonies, or serving in outreach. Provide a safe space to practice, so that disciples grow in courage while receiving support and encouragement. Learning works best when applied, and participation is the key to turning theory into action.

column4: ### Correction
column5: ### Correction

column4: Growth often requires correction, and Jesus lovingly corrected His disciples when they misunderstood His teachings or failed in their tasks. In Mark 9:33-37, He addressed their pride by teaching them about servant leadership. In Luke 22:31-32, He prayed for Peter, preparing Him to recover from failure and strengthen others.
column5: Growth often requires correction, and when disciples misunderstood His teaching or failed in their tasks, Jesus corrected them with compassion. In Mark 9:33-37, He addressed their pride by teaching servant leadership. In Luke 22:31-32, He prayed for Peter, preparing him to recover from failure and strengthen others.

column4: Correction in discipleship should be grace-filled and constructive-rooted in Scripture and aimed at restoration (2 Timothy 4:2). It is not about condemnation but about helping disciples grow and avoid pitfalls. Disciple-makers should provide accountability, using God’s Word to guide and encourage growth while modeling humility in receiving correction themselves.
column5: Correction in discipleship should be full of grace and constructive-rooted in Scripture and aimed at restoration (2 Timothy 4:2). It is not condemnation, but helping disciples grow and avoid pitfalls. Disciplers should provide accountability, use God's Word to guide and encourage growth, while modeling humility in receiving correction themselves.

column4: ### Empowerment/Authorization
column5: ### Empowerment/Authorization

column4: Jesus didn’t just teach and correct- He empowered His disciples to carry out His mission. He gave them authority to preach the Gospel, heal the sick, and cast out demons (Matthew 28:18-20). After His resurrection, He promised the Holy Spirit as the source of power for their ministry (Acts 1:8).
column5: Jesus did not only teach and correct- He also empowered His disciples to carry out His mission. He gave them authority to proclaim the gospel, heal the sick, and cast out demons (Matthew 28:18-20). After His resurrection, He promised the Holy Spirit as the source of power for their ministry (Acts 1:8).

column4: Modern discipleship should include empowering others to operate in their spiritual gifts and minister effectively. This involves identifying gifts (Ephesians 4:11-13), encouraging their use, and releasing disciples to serve. Empowerment also emphasizes reliance on the Holy Spirit for strength, boldness, and wisdom, ensuring disciples are spiritually equipped for the work God has called them to do.
column5: Modern discipleship should include enabling others to operate in their spiritual gifts and serve effectively. This includes identifying gifts (Ephesians 4:11-13), encouraging their use, and releasing disciples to serve. Empowerment also emphasizes relying on the strength, boldness, and wisdom given by the Holy Spirit, ensuring disciples are spiritually equipped to accomplish the work God has called them to do.

column4: ### Multiplication
column5: ### Multiplication

column4: The goal of discipleship isn’t just personal growth-it’s multiplication. Jesus modeled this by training the disciples to make more disciples (Matthew 28:19-20). After His resurrection, the apostles continued this multiplying mission, spreading the Gospel and planting churches across the known world. Paul’s instructions in 2 Timothy 2:2 reinforce this principle, urging Timothy to teach others who will teach others.
column5: The goal of discipleship is not merely personal growth- but multiplication. Jesus modeled this by training disciples to make more disciples (Matthew 28:19-20). After His resurrection, the apostles continued this multiplying mission, spreading the gospel and planting churches across the known world. Paul's instruction in 2 Timothy 2:2 reinforces this principle, urging Timothy to teach those who will teach others.

column4: Discipleship involves equipping disciples to disciple others, creating a chain reaction of faith that expands the Kingdom of God. This process requires intentionality-teaching disciples how to mentor, teach, and train others, while sending them out with confidence and purpose (Romans 10:15).
column5: Discipleship involves equipping disciples to make others, forming a chain reaction of faith that expands God's kingdom. This process requires intentionality- teaching disciples how to mentor, teach, and train others, while sending them out with confidence and purpose (Romans 10:15).

column4: ### Remain Connected
column5: ### Staying Connected

column4: Discipleship doesn’t end when someone is sent out. Jesus modeled ongoing connection with His disciples, continuing to encourage and instruct them even after His resurrection (John 21:15-19). The early church maintained this pattern, gathering regularly for teaching, fellowship, and prayer (Acts 2:42-47).
column5: Discipleship does not end when someone is sent out. Jesus modeled ongoing connection with His disciples, continuing to encourage and teach them even after His resurrection (John 21:15-19). The early church continued this pattern, frequently gathering for teaching, fellowship, and prayer (Acts 2:42-47).

column4: Modern discipleship should also foster ongoing relationships, providing accountability, encouragement, and support as disciples continue to grow and lead. Maintaining unity in the Body of Christ ensures that disciples are never isolated but remain strengthened and encouraged in their faith journey.
column5: Modern discipleship should also cultivate ongoing relationships, providing accountability, encouragement, and support as disciples continue to grow and lead others. Maintaining unity within the body of Christ ensures that disciples are never isolated, but are continually strengthened and encouraged in their journey of faith.

column4: ## Who does Discipleship?
column5: ## Who Does Discipleship?

column4: Everyone in the body of Christ is responsible first to become a disciple, then to contribute to the process of discipleship making. There are diversities of gifts and functions, so our contributions may look different, but we are all responsible. The people ultimately most responsible for the state and health of discipleship in the local church are the leaders (**elders and deacons - Acts 14:23**), but everyone plays a part.
column5: In the body of Christ, everyone is first responsible to be a disciple and then to contribute to the disciple-making process. Gifts and roles are diverse, so our contributions may differ, but we all share responsibility. Those ultimately most responsible for the state and health of discipleship in the local church are the leaders (**elders and deacons - Acts 14:23**), but everyone is to participate.

column4: Discipleship is a living, growing process-like nurturing a child to maturity. Healthy discipleship brings strength and life to people. Like a parent who strengthens and nourishes a child, and in doing so causes them to be healthy and mature, disciple-makers to help nourish, strengthen, and mature disciples. The end goal of discipleship is not ‘knowledge transfer’, but transformation.
column5: Discipleship is a living, growing process- like nurturing children toward maturity. Healthy discipleship brings strength and life. Just as parents strengthen and nourish children so that they grow healthy and mature, disciplers also help to nourish, strengthen, and mature disciples. The ultimate goal of discipleship is not 'transfer of knowledge,' but transformation of life.

column4: All of us must become perfect (mature) and make disciples. While we will have diverse gifts there are common characteristics for all disciple-makers.
column5: We must all become complete (mature) people and make disciples. Although our gifts differ, all disciplers share common qualities.

column4: ### Characteristics of a Disciple-Maker
column5: ### Qualities of a Discipler

column4: A disciple-maker is someone who not only follows Christ but is also committed to helping others grow in their faith. This role requires specific characteristics that reflect both spiritual maturity and practical dedication. Disciple-makers must continually rely on God’s strength, wisdom, and grace to overcome the challenges that come with leading others in their spiritual journeys.
column5: A discipler not only follows Christ personally but is committed to helping others grow in faith. This role requires certain qualities that reflect spiritual maturity as well as practical dedication. Disciplers must continually rely on God's strength, wisdom, and grace to overcome the challenges that accompany leading others on their spiritual journey.

column4: #### Rooted in Christ
column5: #### Rooted in Christ

column4: The foundation of a disciple-maker’s life must be deeply rooted in Christ. Jesus said, *“I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing”* (John 15:5). Effective disciple-makers know that the ability to grow and help others comes from staying close to Jesus every day. However, resistance to personal growth and spiritual change can hinder this dependence. Disciple-makers must continually cultivate their personal relationship with Jesus through prayer, study of Scripture, and obedience, modeling what it means to abide in Christ for those they are discipling.
column5: The life foundation of a disciple maker must be deeply rooted in Christ. Jesus said, “I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing” (John 15:5). Effective disciple makers know that the ability to grow and help others comes from drawing near to Jesus daily. However, resistance to personal growth and spiritual change can hinder this dependence. Disciple makers must continually cultivate their personal relationship with Jesus through prayer, Bible study, and obedience, modeling for the disciples they lead what it means to abide in Christ.

column4: #### Committed to the Mission
column5: #### Faithful to the Mission

column4: A disciple-maker must remain committed to the mission of making disciples as commanded by Jesus in the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20). This mission requires intentional focus and prioritization, recognizing that disciple-making is not an optional task but the core purpose of the church. Yet, challenges such as time constraints, busyness, and personal distractions can make it difficult to stay focused. Disciple-makers must intentionally schedule time for mentoring, teaching, and relationship-building, viewing disciple-making as a lifestyle rather than an occasional activity (Luke 19:10).
column5: Disciple makers must hold fast to the commitment to the mission of making disciples, which Jesus commanded in the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20). This mission requires intentional focus and prioritization, recognizing that making disciples is not an optional task but the church’s core purpose. However, challenges such as time constraints, busyness, and personal distractions can make it difficult to remain focused. Disciple makers must intentionally schedule time for mentoring, teaching, and building relationships, seeing disciple making as a lifestyle rather than an occasional activity (Luke 19:10).

column4: #### Spirit-Led
column5: #### Led by the Holy Spirit

column4: Disciple-making cannot be accomplished in human strength alone; it requires the guidance and empowerment of the Holy Spirit. Jesus promised His disciples that they would receive power when the Holy Spirit came upon them (Acts 1:8), equipping them to be witnesses and ministers of the Gospel. Disciple-makers must be sensitive to the Spirit’s leading, relying on His wisdom to navigate complex situations, cultural barriers, and difficult conversations. This reliance on the Holy Spirit enables disciple-makers to operate in love, boldness, and spiritual discernment, ensuring their efforts are Spirit-directed rather than self-directed.
column5: Making disciples cannot be done by human strength alone; it requires the Holy Spirit’s guidance and empowerment. Jesus promised His disciples that when the Holy Spirit came upon them, they would receive power (<span class="x-scripture" data-book="ACT" data-chapter="1" data-lang="en" data-type="ref" data-verses="8" data-version="NKJV" dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Acts 1:8</span]), enabling them to be witnesses and servants of the gospel. Disciple makers must be sensitive to the Spirit’s leading, relying on His wisdom to navigate complex situations, cultural barriers, and difficult conversations. Dependence on the Holy Spirit enables disciple makers to act in love, courage, and spiritual discernment, ensuring their efforts are Spirit-led rather than self-driven.

column4: #### Humble and Teachable
column5: #### Humble and Teachable

column4: Humility is a hallmark of an effective disciple-maker. As Paul instructed, *“Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves”* (Philippians 2:3). Disciple-makers recognize that they, too, are lifelong learners who must remain teachable and accountable. They invite correction and feedback, modeling humility for those they mentor. Pride can be a significant barrier to growth, both for disciple-makers and their disciples. Embracing accountability and maintaining a servant’s heart fosters trust and creates an environment for growth and transparency.
column5: Humility is the mark of an effective disciple maker. As Paul taught, “Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves” (Philippians 2:3). Disciple makers recognize that they themselves are lifelong learners who must remain teachable and willing to be admonished. They intentionally invite correction and feedback, modeling humility for those they lead. Pride can become a major obstacle to growth, both for disciple makers and for disciples. Embracing mutual accountability and maintaining a servant’s heart helps build trust and fosters an environment conducive to growth and transparency.

column4: #### Patient and Persistent
column5: #### Patient and Persevering

column4: Discipleship is rarely instantaneous-it is a long-term process that requires patience and persistence. Paul reminds believers to *“not grow weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up”* (Galatians 6:9). Growth in faith often involves setbacks, questions, and failures, but disciple-makers are called to walk alongside others, offering encouragement and support through every step. It is easy to become discouraged when progress seems slow, but disciple-makers trust that God is at work, even when results are not immediately visible.
column5: Discipleship is rarely instantaneous-it is a long-term process that requires patience and perseverance. Paul reminds believers, “not grow weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up” (Galatians 6:9). Growth in faith is often accompanied by setbacks, questions, and failures, but disciple makers are called to walk with others, offering encouragement and support at every step. When progress seems slow, it is easy to grow discouraged, but disciple makers trust that God is at work even when results are not immediately visible.

column4: Being a disciple-maker requires a blend of spiritual dependence, commitment, and humility. It is a calling that demands patience and persistence while remaining Spirit-led and teachable. Disciple-makers are not expected to be perfect, but they must be faithful-abiding in Christ, investing in others, and trusting God to bring the growth and transformation in His timing. These qualities reflect Christ’s love and help others become mature disciples who, in turn, can disciple others.
column5: Becoming a disciple maker requires a blend of spiritual dependence, commitment, and humility. It is a calling that demands patience and perseverance while remaining Spirit-led and teachable. Disciple makers are not expected to be perfect, but they must be faithful—abiding in Christ, investing in others, and trusting God to bring growth and transformation in His timing. These qualities reflect Christ’s love and help others become mature disciples who can in turn make others.

column4: ## Practical Tools for Discipleship
column5: ## Practical Tools for Discipleship

column4: Effective discipleship requires intentional tools and practices that foster spiritual growth, accountability, and community. These tools help disciples develop a strong foundation in faith, grow in intimacy with God, and become equipped to disciple others. Practical methods such as Bible study, prayer, small groups, and mentorship provide both the structure and support needed for ongoing growth.
column5: Effective discipleship requires intentional tools and practices that foster spiritual growth, accountability, and community. These tools help disciples build a solid foundation of faith, deepen intimacy with God, and equip them to disciple others. Practical methods such as Bible study, prayer, small groups, and mentoring provide the structure and support needed for sustained growth.

column4: ### Biblical Study
column5: ### Bible Study

column4: Engaging deeply with Scripture is the foundation of discipleship. Jesus emphasized the importance of God’s Word in spiritual growth, declaring that *“man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God”* (Matthew 4:4). Regular Bible study and memorization enable disciples to internalize truth, combat falsehoods, and apply God’s wisdom to daily life.
column5: Deep engagement with Scripture is the foundation of discipleship. Jesus emphasized the importance of God’s Word in spiritual growth, declaring, “man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God” (Matthew 4:4). Regular Bible study and memorization enable disciples to internalize truth, resist error, and apply God’s wisdom to daily life.

column4: Disciples must be encouraged to immerse themselves in Scripture, not merely as an academic exercise but to know God and transform their hearts (Psalms 119:105). Practical approaches, such as reading plans, study guides, and group discussions, provide opportunities to explore doctrine and discuss application in community. By building habits of regular study, disciples lay a solid foundation for spiritual maturity and fruitful ministry (2 Timothy 3:16-17).
column5: Disciples should be encouraged to immerse themselves in Scripture, not merely as an academic exercise but to know God and transform their hearts (Psalm 119:105). Practical approaches such as reading plans, study guides, and group discussion provide opportunities to explore doctrine and discuss application in community. By establishing a habit of regular study, disciples lay a solid foundation for spiritual maturity and effective ministry (2 Timothy 3:16-17).

column4: ### Prayer
column5: ### Prayer

column4: Prayer is the lifeline of discipleship, connecting believers to God’s presence, power, and guidance. Jesus taught His disciples how to pray in Luke 11:1-4, emphasizing both dependence on God and spiritual alignment with His will. Through prayer, disciples learn to seek God’s wisdom, intercede for others, and receive strength for ministry.
column5: Prayer is the lifeline of discipleship, connecting believers with God’s presence, power, and guidance. Jesus taught His disciples how to pray in Luke 11:1-4, emphasizing dependence on God and spiritual alignment with His will. Through prayer, disciples learn to seek God’s wisdom, intercede for others, and receive strength for service.

column4: Teaching disciples how to pray-both individually and corporately-equips them to cultivate intimacy with God and discern His leading (Philippians 4:6-7). Incorporating prayer journals, prayer groups, and fasting practices fosters spiritual discipline and empowerment, ensuring disciples remain Spirit-led and mission-focused.
column5: Teaching disciples how to pray-whether individually or corporately-equips them to cultivate intimacy with God and discern His leading (Philippians 4:6-7). Incorporating practices such as prayer journals, prayer groups, and fasting helps cultivate spiritual discipline and empowerment, ensuring disciples remain Spirit-led and focused on the mission.

column4: ### Small Groups and Community
column5: ### Small Groups and Community

column4: Discipleship thrives in community. The early church modeled relational discipleship through fellowship, prayer, and breaking bread together (Acts 2:42-47). Small groups and accountability partnerships provide a safe space for disciples to grow together, share struggles, and celebrate victories.
column5: Discipleship thrives in community. The early church modeled relational discipleship through fellowship, prayer, and the breaking of bread (Acts 2:42-47). Small groups and accountability partnerships provide safe spaces for disciples to grow together, share struggles, and celebrate victories.

column4: The local church serves as the central hub for discipleship relationships, offering opportunities for group Bible studies, prayer meetings, and fellowship events. These gatherings allow disciples to practice love, bear one another’s burdens (Galatians 6:2), and encourage one another toward spiritual maturity (Hebrews 10:24-25). Small groups also provide a framework for multiplying leaders, as mature disciples train and send others to lead groups and mentor new believers.
column5: The local church is the central hub of discipleship relationships， providing opportunities such as small group Bible studies、prayer meetings、and fellowship activities。 These gatherings enable disciples to practice love， bear one another’s burdens（Galatians 6:2）， and encourage one another toward spiritual maturity（Hebrews 10:24-25）。 Small groups also provide a framework for multiplying leaders， as mature disciples train and send others to lead groups、mentor new believers。

column4: ### Mentorship
column5: ### Mentoring

column4: Mentorship provides a personal and intentional approach to discipleship. Jesus modeled this by investing deeply in the twelve disciples, walking with them through teaching, correction, and encouragement. Similarly, one-on-one relationships allow disciple-makers to tailor guidance to individual needs, helping disciples develop in faith, character, and leadership.
column5: Mentoring provides a personal and intentional approach to discipleship。 Jesus modeled this， investing deeply in the twelve disciples， walking with them through teaching、correction、and encouragement。 Likewise， one-on-one relationships allow disciple-makers to tailor guidance to individual needs， helping disciples grow in faith、character、and leadership。

column4: Mentors serve as accountability partners, offering support, prayer, and wisdom during times of growth and struggle. Practical tools like spiritual assessments, goal-setting, and regular check-ins ensure that disciples stay focused and motivated. Peer relationships within mentorship structures also foster mutual growth, as both mentor and disciple learn from shared experiences (Proverbs 27:17).

column4: ## **Personal Reflection Questions**
column5: ## **Personal Reflection Questions**

column5: 1.  What does being a disciple of Jesus mean to you personally？ How do you actively follow Him in daily life？

column4: 2.  Reflect on Jesus’ model of discipleship. Which aspect of His approach-inviting, teaching, demonstrating, or empowering-stands out most to you, and why?
column5: 2.  Reflect on Jesus’ model of discipleship。 Among His approaches - inviting、teaching、modeling， or empowering - which aspect impresses you the most？ Why？

column4: 3.  How can you multiply your faith by discipling others? What challenges or fears might hold you back, and how can you overcome them? (Notice I said multiply your faith, not multiply your disciples!)
column5: 3.  How can you multiply your faith by leading others to become disciples？ What challenges or fears might hinder you， and how will you overcome them？（Note, I said multiply your faith, not multiply your disciples!）

column4: 4.  What characteristics of a disciple-maker (e.g., patience, humility, relational focus) do you see in yourself? Which traits do you feel led to develop further?
column5: 4.  What qualities of a disciple-maker do you see in yourself（for example， patience、humility、valuing relationships）？ Which qualities do you feel need further development？

column4: 5.  Think about the people in your life. Who might God be calling you to disciple? How can you take the first step in building that relationship?
column5: 5.  Think about the people in your life。 Whom might God be calling you to lead as a disciple？ How can you take the first step to build that relationship？
